body:
## What happened

A wyrd bundle's Check beat sat on the `C5-mutants` row for **19 hours 16 minutes** before a human noticed and interrupted it. The row is `gating = false` — advisory by policy — yet it held the entire beat, and the cycle produced nothing in that window.

```
   56.4s  run{phase=Test}: start  cargo test --package=… (cargo-mutants baseline)
69359.5s  run{phase=Test}: interrupted        ← 19h 15m 59s later, by hand
```

The underlying command was hung on a deadlock in the target project's test suite (a separate bug, filed there). That will happen again, in some project, on some gate: **the engine has no way to bound a gate at all.**

## Mechanism

`gates._run_one` invokes the gate through `progress.run_with_heartbeat` and passes no bound (`gates.py:409`):

```python
rc, output, _ = progress.run_with_heartbeat(
    cmd, cwd=cwd, shell=True, env=_merged_env(env), capture=True, label=label,
    status=lambda: progress.bundle_activity(watch),
)
```

`run_with_heartbeat` has **no `timeout` parameter** in its signature (`progress.py`), and the check schema has no per-gate timeout field. `interval` is only the heartbeat tick. So there is no bound anywhere in the chain.

There is a bitter irony in the comment directly above that call:

> `# Output is captured for the evidence line; the heartbeat ticks meanwhile so`
> `# a long, silent gate (e.g. a Docker-backed test suite) doesn't look hung.`

The heartbeat ticked for nineteen hours. The mechanism built so a slow gate would not look hung is exactly what stopped a genuinely hung gate from looking hung. A human watching the console saw `… still working` and reasonably assumed mutation analysis was just slow.

## Proposal

1. Add `timeout: int | None = None` to `run_with_heartbeat`. On expiry, terminate the child process **group** (gates run under `shell=True`, so killing only the shell orphans the real work), then return a distinguishable outcome.
2. Add an optional `timeout_secs` to the `[[gates.checks]]` schema, plus a `[gates] default_timeout_secs` fallback so a project gets a bound without annotating every row.
3. Record a timed-out row as **`unverifiable`**, not `fail` — "the oracle did not answer" is precisely what `unverifiable` (#46) exists to express, and it keeps a timeout out of the gating verdict while still surfacing at sign-off. Evidence line should name the bound: `gate exceeded its 3600s timeout`.
4. Consider a heartbeat that escalates its wording past some multiple of the expected duration, so `… still working (19h)` reads as alarming rather than routine.

## Why it matters beyond one lost night

An advisory row that can consume unbounded wall-clock is not advisory in any meaningful sense — it has a veto over the whole cycle, just expressed as latency instead of a red verdict. The gating policy in `pdca.toml` reasons carefully about which rows may *block* a fix; it has nothing to say about which rows may *stop time*.
title: gates: a gate command has no timeout — one hung gate stalls the Check beat indefinitely
